best-broadway-shows.intro:
# Best Broadway Shows in March 2026

Broadway enters March 2026 with a remarkably diverse lineup that spans revolutionary modern musicals, timeless revivals, and unexpected comedic gems. This month's top ten shows average an impressive 83/100 critic score, reflecting a theater district firing on all cylinders with productions that range from the groundbreaking to the gloriously absurd.

**Hamilton** continues its reign as Broadway's highest-rated show, with critics still celebrating Lin-Manuel Miranda's hip-hop retelling of American history as a transformative work that redefined what musical theater can be. The production maintains its cultural relevance and theatrical innovation more than a decade after its debut.

Meanwhile, **Maybe Happy Ending** emerges as one of the season's most pleasant surprises—a robot love story that critics describe as among Broadway's most original musicals in years, proving that fresh voices and unconventional narratives still have the power to captivate audiences. On the opposite end of the tonal spectrum, **Oh, Mary!** delivers riotous laughs with Cole Escola's absurdist take on Mary Todd Lincoln as a boozy, cabaret-obsessed narcissist, earning some of the season's most enthusiastic raves.

Classic revivals also demonstrate their staying power this month. **The Lion King** and **Chicago** remind audiences why certain productions become institutions, while the timely **Ragtime** revival resonates with contemporary urgency. From the satirical punch of **The Book of Mormon** to the folk-opera beauty of **Hadestown**, the breadth of storytelling styles on display reflects Broadway's artistic vitality.

Whether you're drawn to hip-hop history lessons, tender robot romance, or irreverent comedy, March 2026 offers exceptional options across every theatrical taste.

The enduring appeal of **The Book of Mormon** and **The Lion King** demonstrates that both irreverent satire and family-friendly spectacle maintain their power to captivate audiences years after their premieres.

Whether you're drawn to groundbreaking innovation, timeless spectacle, or star-powered performances, March 2026 presents one of Broadway's strongest lineups in recent memory.

best-broadway-plays.intro:

As Broadway heads into the spring season, the landscape for straight plays offers an intriguing mix of intimate character studies and spectacular technical showcases. This month's selection of four productions averages a solid 77/100 from critics, revealing a theater scene where ambition doesn't always align with execution, but standout performances and stagecraft continue to captivate audiences.

Leading the pack is **Oh, Mary!**, Cole Escola's absurdist comedy that reimagines Mary Todd Lincoln as a cabaret-obsessed, hard-drinking narcissist. With an 84/100 rating across 33 reviews, the farce has become the season's critical darling, earning consistent praise for its riotous humor and audacious premise. The show proves that original comedic voices still have the power to break through on Broadway.

**Harry Potter and the Cursed Child** maintains its position as a technical marvel, scoring 82/100 from 69 critics. While reviewers note an uneven narrative, the production's magical illusions and spectacular stagecraft continue to justify its status as one of Broadway's most visually ambitious undertakings. The show demonstrates how theatrical innovation can elevate familiar material, even when the storytelling doesn't quite match the spectacle.

At the other end of the spectrum, **Stranger Things: The First Shadow** struggles with its three-hour runtime despite impressive special effects, while **Every Brilliant Thing** enters the rankings with limited critical coverage.

Whether you're drawn to sharp-witted comedy, magical spectacle, or intimate storytelling, this month's offerings provide distinct theatrical experiences worth considering for your Broadway calendar.

The remaining lineup features established Disney properties and popular musicals. **Aladdin** (71/100) delivers visual spectacle in a traditional Broadway package, while **Wicked** (70/100) continues to draw multi-generational audiences with its powerhouse vocals and elaborate production design. **& Juliet** (71/100) offers a contemporary jukebox musical approach that may resonate more with tweens and teens, and **MJ The Musical** (70/100) showcases impressive choreography that appeals to young dance enthusiasts.

best-new-broadway-shows.intro:

Leading the pack is a revival of **Ragtime**, which earns strong critical acclaim for its timely resonance and Joshua Henry's commanding central performance. Critics consistently praise how the production's themes echo contemporary conversations, while the Flaherty and Ahrens score continues to deliver emotional impact decades after its debut.

On the opposite end of the theatrical spectrum, **Two Strangers (Carry a Cake Across New York)** proves that Broadway has room for small-scale storytelling. This British import wins over reviewers with its modest ambitions and sincere performances, offering audiences a heartfelt alternative to the season's larger spectacles.

The month's most polarizing entry is **Chess**, where critical opinion splits sharply. While the ABBA-penned score and powerhouse vocal performances from Lea Michele, Aaron Tveit, and the ensemble earn consistent praise, reviewers remain divided on the production's overall execution and the musical's famously unwieldy book.

With an average critical score of 75 across the featured productions, March presents a solid if somewhat uneven theatrical landscape. The range—from Ragtime's sweeping historical drama to Two Strangers' intimate simplicity—offers theatergoers varied options depending on their appetite for scale and subject matter. Whether you're drawn to socially resonant revivals or quieter character studies, this month's Broadway offerings provide multiple entry points for different tastes.

best-broadway-shows-2020.intro:

As we look back in March 2026 at the Broadway shows that premiered in 2020, we're examining a theatrical landscape dramatically shaped by the pandemic's abrupt shutdown that spring. The shows that managed to open before Broadway went dark represent a fascinating cross-section of ambitious revivals and intimate dramas that were cut short in their original runs.

Leading our rankings is a rebooted **Les Misérables** at the refurbished Sondheim Theatre, earning an 83/100 from critics who largely embrace its grittier aesthetic, though the production hasn't won universal acclaim. Close behind, **A Soldier's Play** stands out as a critical highlight, scoring 78/100 for its powerful staging of Charles Fuller's Pulitzer-winning drama—a work that proved remarkably resonant in its long-overdue Broadway premiere.

The year's offerings skew toward smaller-scale productions, with **My Name is Lucy Barton** showcasing Laura Linney in a solo performance that divides critics despite widespread admiration for the star's work. Meanwhile, **Grand Horizons** delivers familiar boulevard comedy territory elevated by veteran performers Jane Alexander and company, and Ivo van Hove's **West Side Story** reimagining proves predictably polarizing, with its radical video-heavy approach earning both passionate advocates and detractors.

With an average critical score of 74/100 across these five productions, the 2020 Broadway season—brief as it was—offered more solid craftsmanship than groundbreaking innovation. For theatergoers and students of Broadway history, these shows represent both the artistic ambitions of a pre-pandemic era and a poignant reminder of the fragility of live performance.

best-broadway-shows-2021.intro:
# Best Broadway Shows from 2021

As we look back from March 2026, the Broadway shows that opened in 2021 represent a remarkable chapter in theater history—the season that brought live performance roaring back to life after the pandemic shutdown. These productions, now five years old, range from experimental docudramas to beloved mega-musicals, and collectively they earn an impressive 81/100 average critic score.

The highest-rated show from this cohort remains **Dana H.**, Lucas Hnath's unconventional docudrama featuring Deirdre O'Connell's stunning lip-sync performance. Critics continue to describe it as mesmerizing and unforgettable, a testament to theater's capacity for innovation. Close behind, **The Phantom of the Opera** proves that Andrew Lloyd Webber's mega-musical spectacle still captivates audiences with its infectious melodies and grand production values, even if some critics find it campy. Meanwhile, **Cabaret at the Kit Kat Club** earns widespread acclaim for Rebecca Frecknall's immersive reimagining that transforms the entire Playhouse Theatre into a pre-war nightclub.

The 2021 season also brought powerful solo performances like Ruben Santiago-Hudson's virtuosic **Lackawanna Blues**, verbatim theater experiments such as **Is This a Room**, and significant revivals including Marianne Elliott's gender-swapped **Company**. Antoinette Chinonye Nwandu's **Pass Over** holds special significance as Broadway's official reopening production, while **The Lehman Trilogy** delivers epic scope and **SIX** offers pure pop exuberance.

Whether you're seeking experimental boundary-pushing work or classic Broadway spectacle, the class of 2021 offers exceptional variety and quality that continues to resonate with audiences today.

best-broadway-plays-2020.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays from 2020

As we look back from March 2026, the Broadway plays that opened in 2020 represent a fascinating snapshot of theater interrupted—productions that launched just before or during one of the most turbulent periods in Broadway history. These five shows, averaging a solid 74/100 critical score, showcase a season that balanced ambitious revivals with intimate character studies.

**Les Misérables** leads the pack with an 83/100, as this grittier reboot at the refurbished Sondheim Theatre reimagines the beloved musical classic with a darker edge that resonates with most critics, even as some purists remain unconvinced. **A Soldier's Play** follows closely at 78/100, bringing Charles Fuller's Pulitzer Prize-winning drama to Broadway for the first time in a revival that critics hail as both powerful and long overdue, proving the work's examination of race and military justice remains urgently relevant.

The remaining three productions demonstrate the season's range. Laura Linney anchors **My Name is Lucy Barton** in a solo performance critics universally admire, though opinions split on the adaptation itself. **Grand Horizons** offers more traditional fare—a boulevard comedy about late-life divorce elevated by veteran performers Jane Alexander and James Cromwell. Meanwhile, Ivo van Hove's **West Side Story** proves the most polarizing entry, with its radical staging choices earning both passionate advocacy and sharp criticism.

Together, these productions reflect a moment when Broadway was taking creative risks, reviving essential American dramas, and reimagining classics through contemporary lenses. For theatergoers interested in this pivotal season, these five plays offer essential viewing to understand where Broadway stood at a critical juncture.

best-broadway-plays-2021.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays of 2021

As we look back from March 2026, the Broadway shows that opened in 2021 represent a remarkable chapter in theater history—productions that not only marked the industry's resilient return from pandemic shutdown but also pushed creative boundaries in unexpected ways.

The ten productions featured here achieve an impressive average critic score of 81/100, reflecting a season of exceptional artistic ambition. Leading the field is **Dana H.**, Lucas Hnath's unconventional docudrama that continues to mesmerize audiences with Deirdre O'Connell's stunning lip-sync performance, earning an 86/100 from critics who describe it as unforgettable theater. Close behind, **Cabaret at the Kit Kat Club** (83/100) demonstrates how Rebecca Frecknall's immersive reimagining can breathe new life into a classic, transforming the Playhouse Theatre itself into an essential part of the experience.

The season's range proves remarkable: from **The Lehman Trilogy**'s epic three-hour examination of American capitalism to **Is This a Room**'s taut 70-minute verbatim thriller drawn from FBI transcripts. Antoinette Chinonye Nwandu's **Pass Over** earned its place in history as the first play to reopen Broadway, while Stephen Sondheim's **Company** arrived in a gender-swapped revival that critics embraced as vital and dazzling.

These productions—whether intimate solo performances like **Lackawanna Blues**, exuberant pop spectacles like **SIX**, or the final years of **The Phantom of the Opera**'s record-breaking run—showcase the breadth of theatrical storytelling that defined Broadway's comeback year. For theatergoers exploring what's still running or planning future visits, these critic-approved productions offer a guide to 2021's most accomplished work.

best-broadway-plays-2022.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays That Opened in 2022

As we look back from March 2026, the 2022 Broadway season stands out as a remarkable year that brought both innovative new voices and masterful revivals to the stage. The shows that debuted during this period continue to resonate with audiences, many still running strong nearly four years later.

Leading the class is **Kimberly Akimbo**, the quirky musical about a teenager with a rare aging condition that critics hail as a near-perfect gem, balancing hilarious comedy with aching poignancy. Close behind, **Into the Woods** proves that Sondheim's genius endures, with this stripped-down revival earning widespread acclaim as a triumphant tribute to the late composer. **A Strange Loop**, Michael R. Jackson's Pulitzer Prize-winning meta-musical, rounds out the top tier with its brazenly original and brutally honest exploration of Black queer identity.

What distinguishes 2022's offerings is the remarkable concentration of Pulitzer Prize-winning works. The season brought revivals of **Topdog/Underdog**, **Between Riverside and Crazy**, **How I Learned to Drive**, and **Cost of Living** to Broadway stages, alongside **Leopoldstadt**, Tom Stoppard's deeply personal Holocaust meditation. This convergence of America's most celebrated dramatic voices created an unusually rich theatrical landscape.

The season also showcased diversity in form, from Mike Birbiglia's masterful solo storytelling in **The Old Man & The Pool** to Jordan E. Cooper's audacious sketch-comedy satire **Ain't No Mo'**. With an average critic score of 83/100 across these ten productions, the 2022 season represents a high-water mark for Broadway quality. Whether you're catching these shows during their extended runs or discovering them for the first time, this collection offers some of the finest theatrical experiences currently available.

best-broadway-plays-2023.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays of 2023

As of March 2026, the Broadway plays that debuted in 2023 continue to demonstrate the exceptional artistic vitality of that season, with an impressive average critic score of 82/100 across our featured productions.

The year proved particularly significant for revivals that recontextualized classic works for contemporary audiences. Maria Friedman's production of **Merrily We Roll Along** stands as the highest-rated play from 2023, earning widespread acclaim for finally unlocking the emotional power of Sondheim's once-maligned musical. The production transforms what was considered a notorious failure into a triumph of theatrical storytelling. Similarly, **Parade** resonates with urgent relevance, while Branden Jacobs-Jenkins's **Appropriate** earns recognition as a modern masterpiece, with Sarah Paulson leading a blistering ensemble through a searing family drama.

The season also showcases remarkable range, from the long-overdue revival of Ossie Davis's satirical **Purlie Victorious** to the intimate brilliance of Alex Edelman's solo show **Just for Us**. Pulitzer Prize winner **Fat Ham** brings fresh perspective to Shakespearean adaptation, while **Stranger Things: The First Shadow** proves that technically ambitious spectacle can transcend its source material. Traditional musical revivals like **Sweeney Todd** demonstrate that full-scale productions of canonical works still command critical respect, while **Buena Vista Social Club** and the immersive **Stereophonic** expand the boundaries of theatrical storytelling.

Whether you're drawn to innovative revivals, intimate solo performances, or ambitious new works, these ten productions represent the best theatrical experiences that 2023's Broadway season continues to offer audiences today.

best-broadway-plays-2025.intro:

Close behind, **The 25th Annual Putnam County Spelling Bee** returns for its 20th anniversary, with critics celebrating this revival as both joyous and perfectly timed. The musical's airtight writing and emotional depth remind audiences why this quirky show about adolescent spelling champions became a beloved modern classic.

Meanwhile, ambitious new works like Sanaz Toossi's Pulitzer Prize-winning **English** and Branden Jacobs-Jenkins' **Purpose** showcase contemporary playwrights grappling with questions of identity, language, and family dynamics.

The season's range extends from the timely social commentary of **Ragtime** to the darkly comic absurdism of **Dead Outlaw**, proving that Broadway's dramatic offerings serve diverse tastes and perspectives. Whether you're drawn to classic American drama, innovative new voices, or heartwarming spectacle, this collection of plays offers compelling reasons to experience live theater at its finest.
